title: Hover, tap and focus feedback
description: Give buttons, links and cards hover, press and focus feedback that behaves correctly on touch, and reveal content as it scrolls into view.

Interaction directives animate **while** something is true — the pointer is over the element, it is pressed, it has focus — and reverse when it stops. They follow their inputs after initialisation, so a bound value can change at any time.

## Buttons and links

:::code buy-button.ts

```ts
@Component({
  selector: 'app-buy-button',
  imports: [MoveHoverDirective, MoveTapDirective],
  template: `
    <!-- lift = a 4px rise (translate), press = a 3% scale-down. Separate channels, so they compose. -->
    <button type="button" moveWhileHover="lift" moveWhileTap="press">Buy now</button>
  `,
})
export class BuyButton {}
```

[View source](https://github.com/Andersseen/angular-movement/blob/main/src/docs-snippets/interactions.ts#L10-L18)

`lift` and `press` are the two interaction presets. They write different style channels (`translate` and `scale`), so they compose on one element.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Hover means a mouse or a pen: a finger has no hover state, and emulating one is what produces sticky hover and blocked taps. Pair [`MoveHoverDirective`](/docs/reference/move-hover-directive) with [`MoveTapDirective`](/docs/reference/move-tap-directive) so touch gets press feedback. Neither directive calls `preventDefault()`, so links, buttons and scrolling behave natively.

::playground[interaction]

Each control applies immediately, because these directives are reactive. [Open the full hover playground](/demos/hover) or the [tap](/demos/tap) one.

## Focus

[`MoveFocusDirective`](/docs/reference/move-focus-directive) animates while the element has focus. Do not use it as the only focus indicator: keep a visible `:focus-visible` style.

:::code field.ts

```ts
@Component({
  selector: 'app-field',
  imports: [MoveFocusDirective],
  template: `<input [moveWhileFocus]="{ scale: [1, 1.02] }" aria-label="Email" />`,
})
export class Field {}
```

[View source](https://github.com/Andersseen/angular-movement/blob/main/src/docs-snippets/interactions.ts#L22-L27)

## Reveal on scroll

[`MoveInViewDirective`](/docs/reference/move-in-view-directive) plays when an element enters the viewport (once by default). It is one-shot, like `moveEnter`.

:::code product-card.ts

```ts
@Component({
  selector: 'app-product-card',
  imports: [MoveInViewDirective, MoveHoverDirective],
  template: `<article moveInView="fade-up" moveWhileHover="lift">Product</article>`,
})
export class ProductCard {}
```

[View source](https://github.com/Andersseen/angular-movement/blob/main/src/docs-snippets/interactions.ts#L31-L36)

Elements that start hidden and animate in are revealed once the app has booted, so content _below_ the fold is a good fit; keep above-the-fold content visible in the server-rendered HTML.
